title: deferred-cutover-safety-net-with-telemetry-witness
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Improve resilience of multi-stage rollouts by adding a lightweight deferred-cutover safety net and an independent telemetry witness that can veto or pause cutovers when drift or metric anomalies are detected. This change is targeted at complex fanout rollouts (A/B + shadow lanes) where downstream stabilization is latent and automated rollback or holdpoints are required. Design summary: 1) Introduce a Telemetry Witness component that subscribes to rollout events and emits a signed verdict (allow|pause|veto) based on sliding-window metric heuristics and anomaly detectors. 2) Add a Deferred Cutover controller that delays final traffic shift until the witness returns a positive verdict or a timeout elapses; supports operator-configured holdpoints and manual override. 3) Persist a immutable Decision Journal for each rollout with timestamps, witness verdicts, triggering metrics, and the operator who performed any manual override. 4) Provide a packaged rollback playbook and a minimal API for external audit/forensics. Backwards compatibility: witness is opt-in per-rollout via rollout.spec.safety.witness.enabled=false by default; controller falls back to existing immediate-cutover behavior when disabled. Tests: unit tests for verdict logic and timeout behavior, integration e2e test which simulates a drift by introducing synthetic latency and ensuring rollout pauses, and a smoke upgrade test for private deployments. Checklist: - [x] Add witness component and gRPC contract - [x] Implement deferred cutover controller + decision journal - [x] Expose manual override endpoints with RBAC checks - [x] Add e2e integration test and add to CI matrix - [x] Add runbook and rollback playbook docs - [x] Perf sanity: witness runs in separate lightweight goroutine and limits to 50ms latency budget per verdict Related linear tasks: ENG-2145 (telemetry witness PoC), ENG-2210 (deferred cutover design). Rollout lifecycle impact: decision journal enables post-mortem playback for canary/A-B experiments; automated veto reduces blast radius for accidental regressions. Migration notes: existing rollout CRs keep current semantics; to opt-in set spec.safety.witness.enabled: true and configure spec.safety.witness.policyRef. Security: verdicts are signed with controller identity; manual override requires escalation role. CI notes: initial run failed a flaky integration test, fixed by rate-limiting synthetic load in the test harness. Merge: squash and merge after final approval. Release notes: "Add opt-in Telemetry Witness and Deferred Cutover safety-net for rollouts; adds decision journal and a packaged rollback playbook."

conversations: Marcus Li (reviewer): Nice design, can you clarify failure modes when the witness is partitioned?

Asha Patel (author): If witness cannot reach metrics backend within verdict timeout we treat as 'pause' to minimize blast radius; added decision journal entry marking 'witness_unreachable' and an operator alert. See deferred_cutover_controller.go:handleWitnessTimeout
Sofia Martinez (reviewer): Please ensure manual override requires escalate role and is audited.
Asha Patel (author): Manual override now requires role 'rollout.operator.escalate' and writes an audited event to the decision journal. Added integration test for override flow.
Jun Park (approver): Integration e2e passes in CI and manual playbook looks good. Approving.
